title: Command: actions you can undo
summary: Each edit is an object with do() and undo(). The editor keeps two stacks: undo moves the last command from done to undone, redo moves it back, and a new command clears redo.
code: # Every edit knows how to undo itself; two stacks give undo and redo.
triggers: undo and redo, macros, or a log of user actions that must be stored and replayed
separate what triggers an action (a button, shortcut or menu) from the code that performs it
prompts: A drawing app lets users move, recolour and delete shapes, then step backwards and forwards through those changes as far as they like.
A smart-home hub records the actions a scene performs, so one tap can roll the whole scene back in reverse order.
invariant: done holds applied commands in order and undone holds undone ones; undo and redo move one command between them, and a new command empties undone.
mantra: Every action knows its inverse; a new action clears redo.
pitfalls: A new command must clear the redo stack; redoing old commands onto newer text corrupts it.
undo must reverse exactly what do changed: the whole inserted text, at its position.
Undo in reverse order by popping from the end of the history.
